title: USB4-style transport layer adapter: transport layer packets with HEC-protected headers, HEC delineation with single-bit correction, two tunneled paths with HopID routing, credit-based flow control per path

fields.desc: the logical layer is up: Idle packets, then credit grants; clearing it returns delineation to HUNT and restarts credit counts (a packet cut by it is sent again)
paths enabled (bit p: path p sends, accepts its ingress HopID and grants credit)

regs.name: HOP0
regs.desc: Path 0 HopIDs (change them only while the path is disabled)

fields.desc: egress HopID: put in path 0's packets, and matched against credit grants
ingress HopID: packets with it go to path 0

regs.name: HOP1
regs.desc: Path 1 HopIDs (change them only while the path is disabled)

regs.name: TX
regs.desc: Packet byte to send on a path; one write per byte, LAST on the final byte (a packet is cut after MAXL = 32 bytes). Each path has one packet buffer: bytes are taken while the PATH's buffer is free, and the buffer frees once the packet went out (the partner must have granted credit). The two paths' bytes may be interleaved

regs.name: RX
regs.desc: Received packet byte (head of the core's receive buffers, packets in arrival order); reading it pops it. A credit grant is sent once a packet is read out

fdesc.rx_path: the path it came in on

fields.desc: bit p: a credit grant arrived for path p

irqs.name: HEC_FIX
irqs.desc: a header with a single-bit error was corrected

irqs.name: ERR_HEC
irqs.desc: a header HEC error in SYNC that could not be corrected: delineation back to HUNT

irqs.name: ERR_PROTO
irqs.desc: a HopID 0 packet with an unknown PDF or length, or a credit grant with reserved bits set, for no enabled path or over RXB credits ahead

irqs.name: ERR_HOP
irqs.desc: a packet for a HopID of no enabled path: skipped

irqs.name: ERR_LEN
irqs.desc: a data packet with length 0 or over MAXL: skipped

irqs.name: ERR_OVERFLOW
irqs.desc: a data packet for a path whose RXB buffers are full: dropped

notes: tx_sym and rx_sym are the transport layer byte streams (one byte per clock each way while link_up); they pass through unchanged.
The core parameters MAXL (32), RXB (2 buffers per path), DELTA (4) and REFRESH (128) keep their defaults.
